Attached (zipped): enclave-zoning_v1.pdf, control-handshake_sequence.png, kms-boundary_matrix.csv, egress-playbook.md

Executive narrative (summary):
Redwood deploys Dedicated and Private workloads into logically separated enclave layers. Each deployment separates three primary planes: control plane (orchestration & identity), data/compute plane (model inference), and telemetry/observability. Tenant compute runs in isolated host pools (Dedicated) or tenant VPCs (Private) with network-level ACLs and microsegmentation applied at the service edge. Shared services (e.g., centralized monitoring, update orchestration) run in a separate management enclave with tightly scoped peering.

Control-plane handshake (high-level):
- Bootstrap: Host authenticates to Redwood control services using an X.509 certificate provisioned at image creation; initial attestation includes image hash + signed CSR.
- Session: Post-bootstrap, mTLS is established between host agent and control endpoints. Short-lived session tokens (rotated by the control plane) authorize config pulls and model pull requests.
- Rotation / revocation: Certificate rotation is automated on a scheduled window or on explicit revocation events. If rotation fails, the host is quarantined and marked for remediation; failover traffic is routed to standby hosts.

Emergency failover:
- Trigger: host health degradation, kernel-level faults, or degraded I/O to attached model cache triggers automated evacuation.
- State sync: lightweight checkpoints for KV cache and model metadata are streamed to nearby standby nodes; full model artifacts are pulled from the model registry on failover.
- Blast radius mitigation: routing policies isolate failing hosts at the service edge; tenant affinity is maintained where possible and traffic is throttled to maintain upstream SLOs.

KMS/HSM note: The kms-boundary_matrix.csv attached lists which components invoke external KMS, whether keys are customer-managed (BYOK), and typical call flows. In Dedicated we support customer-managed keys for encrypting model artifacts at rest; in Private we support both customer-managed and hardware security modules in-customer-network.

Egress controls:
- Only outbound egress to model registry (HTTPS), telemetry endpoints, and KMS endpoints is allowed from compute hosts.
- Agents use TLS 1.2+ with certificate pinning to known endpoints.
